Arctic Warbler.breeding: Siberian taiga and the Russian Far East
Arctic Warbler.wintering: Southeast Asia, the Philippines and Indonesia
Arctic Warbler.via: Eastern Asia, including China and Taiwan; some return through Mongolia

source.title: University of Copenhagen · Arctic Warbler tracking study

Arctic Warbler.note: The tracking study followed one central Siberian bird; routes differ among populations.

Siberian Rubythroat.breeding: Siberia and the Russian Far East
Siberian Rubythroat.via: Northeast China and the mainland East Asian corridor

source.title: Heim et al. · Full annual cycle tracking of Siberian Rubythroat

Siberian Rubythroat.note: Tracked Amur-region birds wintered in southern China and Indochina. Other populations can use different routes.

Yellow-breasted Bunting.breeding: Siberia, Mongolia and the Russian Far East
Yellow-breasted Bunting.wintering: Southern China, Myanmar, Thailand and other parts of Southeast Asia
Yellow-breasted Bunting.via: China and the mainland East Asian corridor

source.title: Heim et al. · Migration routes of Yellow-breasted Bunting

Yellow-breasted Bunting.note: Tracked Baikal and Amur birds used Southeast Asia and southern China. The wider species range also includes northern India and Nepal.

Rustic Bunting.breeding: The Eurasian taiga, including Siberia and Kamchatka
Rustic Bunting.wintering: Japan, the Korean Peninsula and eastern and central China
Rustic Bunting.via: The Russian Far East and eastern China

source.title: Edenius et al. · Global population decline in Rustic Bunting

Siberian Crane.wintering: Poyang Lake and nearby wetlands in China
Siberian Crane.via: The Aldan and Amur basins, then northeast Chinese wetlands such as Momoge

source.title: Convention on Migratory Species · Eastern Siberian Crane monitoring

Siberian Crane.note: This map covers the eastern population; historic western and central migration routes are outside its scope.

Hooded Crane.breeding: Central and southeastern Russia and northern China
Hooded Crane.wintering: Mainly Izumi in southern Japan; also Korea and China's middle Yangtze wetlands
Hooded Crane.via: Northeast China and the Korean Peninsula

White-naped Crane.breeding: Mongolia, northeast China and the Amur River basin
White-naped Crane.wintering: Poyang Lake in China, or South Korea and southern Japan
White-naped Crane.via: China for western birds; the Korean Peninsula for eastern birds

source.title: Tracking study · Breeding and migration performance of White-naped Cranes

White-naped Crane.note: Western and eastern populations have different wintering grounds. The animation combines their seasonal distributions.

Swan Goose.breeding: Mongolia and adjoining northeast Asian wetlands
Swan Goose.wintering: Wetlands along China's Yangtze River basin
Swan Goose.via: Northeast China, including the Yalu River estuary

source.title: USGS · Migration strategies of Swan Geese from northeast Mongolia

Swan Goose.note: Tracked Mongolian geese staged for weeks at the Yalu estuary before continuing to the Yangtze.

Baikal Teal.breeding: Eastern Siberia, including the Kolyma and lower Lena regions
Baikal Teal.wintering: South Korea, Japan and eastern China
Baikal Teal.via: Northeast China and eastern Russia; several spring corridors are known

source.title: Nam et al. · Three spring migration routes of Baikal Teal

Baikal Teal.note: The cited satellite study followed birds wintering in South Korea.

Great Knot.wintering: Coasts of Southeast Asia and Australia
Great Knot.note: Other wintering populations occur around the northern Indian Ocean.

Red-necked Stint.wintering: Coasts and wetlands of Southeast Asia and Australia
Red-necked Stint.via: Asian wetlands, the Yellow Sea and Indonesian stopovers

source.title: Victorian Wader Study Group · Red-necked Stint tracking

Red-necked Stint.note: Many short flights and varied stopovers connect the breeding and wintering grounds.

Far Eastern Curlew.wintering: Mainly coastal Australia; also Southeast Asian coasts
Far Eastern Curlew.via: Coastal East Asia, including the Yellow Sea
Far Eastern Curlew.note: Birds leave breeding areas from July to September and depart Australia mainly in February and March.
